verses.1:1: The burden that the prophet Habakkuk saw.
verses.1:2: How long, Lord, will I cry out, and You will not listen? Will I shout aloud to You, suffering violence, and You will not save?
verses.1:3: Why have You shown me iniquity and toil, to see plunder and injustice against me? And judgment has come about, and contradiction is more powerful.
verses.1:4: Because of this, the law is torn apart, and judgment does not reach all the way to the end; because the wicked one prevails against the righteous one, therefore perverted judgment goes forth.
verses.1:5: Look among the nations, and see; marvel, and be astounded, for a work has been done in your days that no one will believe when it is told.
verses.1:6: For look, I will raise up the Chaldeans, a bitter and swift nation, walking over the breadth of the earth to possess tents not its own.
verses.1:7: It is dreadful and terrifying; from itself its judgment and its burden will go forth.
verses.1:8: Its horses are lighter than leopards, and swifter than evening wolves; and its horsemen will spread out, for its horsemen will come from afar; they will fly like an eagle hurrying to eat.
verses.1:9: All of them will come for plunder; their face is a burning wind, and it will gather captives like sand.
verses.1:10: And he will triumph over kings, and tyrants will be his laughingstocks; he will laugh at every fortification, and he will pile up a mound and capture it.
verses.1:11: Then the spirit will be changed, and he will pass through and fall; this strength of his is his god's.
verses.1:12: Are You not from the beginning, Lord, my God, my Holy One, and we will not die? Lord, You have appointed him for judgment, and You have established him strong so that You might correct.
verses.1:13: Your eyes are pure, so that You do not see evil, and You will not be able to look upon iniquity. Why do You look upon those who do iniquity, and remain silent while the wicked devours one more righteous than himself?
verses.1:14: And You will make men like the fish of the sea, and like a creeping thing having no ruler.
verses.1:15: He lifted up the whole with a hook, dragged it in his dragnet, and gathered it into his net. Over this he will be glad and exult.
verses.1:16: Therefore he will offer sacrifice to his dragnet and make offerings to his net, because through them his portion has been made fat, and his food is choice.
verses.1:17: Because of this, then, he spreads out his dragnet, and he will not refrain from always killing nations.
verses.2:1: I will stand on my watch, and I will set my step upon the fortification; and I will keep watch to see what is spoken to me, and what I may answer to the one reproving me.
verses.2:2: And the Lord answered me and said, "Write the vision, and make it plain upon tablets, so that the one who reads it may run through it.
verses.2:3: For the vision is still far off, and it will appear at the end, and it will not lie. If it makes a delay, wait for it; for coming it will come, and it will not be late.
verses.2:4: Look, as for the one who is unbelieving, his soul will not be upright within himself; but the righteous one will live in his faith.
verses.2:5: And just as wine deceives the one who drinks, so will the proud man be, and he will not be honored, he who has widened his soul like the underworld, and he himself is like death and is not filled; and he will gather to himself all nations, and heap up to himself all peoples.
verses.2:6: Will not all these take up a parable against him, and a saying of riddles about him? And it will be said, 'Woe to the one who multiplies what is not his! How long does he also load thick clay against himself?
verses.2:7: Will not those who bite you suddenly rise up, and those tearing you apart be roused, and you become prey for them?
verses.2:8: Because you have plundered many nations, all who remain of the peoples will plunder you, because of the blood of man, and the iniquity of the land, of the city, and of all who dwell in it.
verses.2:9: Woe to the one who gathers evil greed for his house, so that his nest may be on high, and thinks that he is delivered from the hand of evil!
verses.2:10: You have devised shame for your house; you have cut down many peoples, and your soul has sinned.
verses.2:11: For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the wood that is between the joints of the buildings will answer.
verses.2:12: Woe to the one who builds a city in bloodshed, and prepares a town in iniquity!
verses.2:13: Are not these things from the Lord of hosts? For the peoples will toil in much fire, and the nations in vain, and they will fail.
verses.2:14: For the earth will be filled so that they may know the glory of the Lord, like waters covering the sea.
verses.2:15: Woe to the one who gives drink to his friend, pouring in his gall, and making him drunk so that he may look upon his nakedness!
verses.2:16: You have been filled with disgrace instead of glory; drink, you too, and fall into a stupor. The cup of the right hand of the Lord will encompass you, and vomit of disgrace will be upon your glory.
verses.2:17: For the iniquity of Lebanon will cover you, and the devastation of animals will terrify them, because of the bloodshed of men, and the iniquity of the land, and of the city, and of all who dwell in it.
verses.2:18: What profit is a carved image, that its maker has carved it, a molten image and a false likeness? For its maker has trusted in his handiwork, to make mute idols.
verses.2:19: Woe to the one who says to wood, "Wake up!" and "Arise!" to a silent stone! Will it be able to teach? Look, it is covered with gold and silver, and there is no spirit at all in its inward parts.'
verses.2:20: But the Lord is in His holy temple; let all the earth be silent before His face!"
verses.3:1: A prayer of the prophet Habakkuk, for ignorances.
verses.3:2: Lord, I have heard Your report, and I was afraid. Lord, Your work, in the midst of the years bring it to life; in the midst of the years You will make it known; when You are angry, You will remember mercy.
verses.3:3: God will come from the south, and the Holy One from Mount Paran; His glory has covered the heavens, and the earth is full of His praise.
verses.3:4: His radiance will be like the light; horns are in His hands; there His strength is hidden.
verses.3:5: Before His face death will go, and the devil will go forth before His feet.
verses.3:6: He stood and measured the earth; He looked and dissolved the nations, and the mountains of the age were crushed; the hills of the world were bowed down by the paths of His eternity.
verses.3:7: Because of iniquity I saw the tents of Ethiopia; the skins of the land of Midian will be troubled.
verses.3:8: Were You angry with the rivers, Lord? Or was Your fury against the rivers, or Your indignation against the sea? For You will ride upon Your horses, and Your chariots are salvation.
verses.3:9: Rousing, You will rouse Your bow, the oaths to the tribes that You have spoken; You will split the rivers of the earth.
verses.3:10: The mountains saw You and were in pain; a torrent of waters passed by; the deep gave its voice; the height lifted up its hands.
verses.3:11: The sun and the moon stood still in their dwelling; in the light of Your arrows they will go, in the radiance of Your flashing spear.
verses.3:12: In rage You will trample the earth; in fury You will astound the nations.
verses.3:13: You went forth for the salvation of Your people, for salvation with Your anointed; You struck the head from the house of the wicked; You laid bare its foundation all the way to the neck.
verses.3:14: You cursed his scepters, the head of his warriors, coming like a whirlwind to scatter me; their exultation was like that of one who devours the poor in secret.
verses.3:15: You made a way in the sea for Your horses, in the mud of many waters.
verses.3:16: I heard, and my belly was troubled; at the voice my lips trembled. Let rottenness enter into my bones and swarm beneath me, so that I may rest in the day of tribulation, so that I may go up to our girded people.
verses.3:17: For the fig tree will not bloom, and there will be no sprout on the vines; the work of the olive will deceive, and the fields will not bring food; the flock will be cut off from the sheepfold, and there will be no herd in the stalls.
verses.3:18: Yet I will rejoice in the Lord, and I will exult in God my Jesus.
verses.3:19: God the Lord is my strength, and He will make my feet like those of deer; and the Victor will lead me, singing in psalms, upon my high places.

notes.1:3: Vulgate 'factum est judicium, et contradictio potentior' ("judgment has come about, and contradiction is more powerful") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which speaks of strife arising and contention lifting up.
notes.1:5: Vulgate uses the passive 'opus factum est' ("a work has been done") and third-person 'nemo credet' ("no one will believe"), where the Hebrew has first-person active ("I am doing a work") and second-person ("you will not believe").
notes.1:11: Vulgate 'corruet' ("will fall") diverges from the Hebrew ("will become guilty"), and the compressed double-genitive clause 'hæc est fortitudo ejus dei sui' ("this strength of his is his god's") attributes the conqueror's power to his god.
notes.1:12: Vulgate reads the accusative 'fortem' ("strong") in reference to the Chaldean invader, whereas the Hebrew 'tsur' ("Rock") is a vocative title addressed to God.
notes.2:4: Vulgate 'qui incredulus est' ("the one who is unbelieving") and 'in fide sua' ("in his faith") differ from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which describes one who is "puffed up" and the righteous living by "his faithfulness."
notes.2:5: Vulgate 'non decorabitur' ("will not be honored") translates Hebrew 'lo yinweh' ("will not stay at home" or "will not endure") via a related root denoting beauty or adornment.
notes.2:6: Vulgate 'densum lutum' ("thick clay") reads Hebrew 'avtit' ("heavy pledges" or "debt") as two words meaning "thick clay."
notes.2:14: Vulgate renders a purpose clause, 'ut cognoscant gloriam Domini' ("so that they may know the glory of the Lord"), rather than the Hebrew noun phrase "with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord."
notes.2:16: Vulgate 'consopire' ("fall into a stupor") reflects a reading meaning "stagger" or "be stunned," rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "be exposed as uncircumcised."
notes.3:1: Vulgate 'pro ignorantiis' ("for ignorances") interprets the obscure Hebrew musical term 'al shigyonot' ("according to Shigionoth") through the verb root meaning to err in ignorance.
notes.3:4: Vulgate 'cornua in manibus ejus' ("horns are in His hands") translates Hebrew 'qarnayim' literally as "horns" rather than "rays" and places them "in His hands."
notes.3:5: Vulgate 'mors' ("death") and 'diabolus' ("the devil") are distinctive Latin renderings of Hebrew 'dever' ("pestilence") and 'reshef' ("plague" or "fiery bolt").
notes.3:7: Vulgate uses the proper name 'Æthiopiæ' ("Ethiopia") for Hebrew 'Kushan', and renders Hebrew 'tachat awen' ("under affliction") as 'Pro iniquitate' ("Because of iniquity").
notes.3:16: Vulgate 'scateat' ("swarm") and 'ut ascendam ad populum accinctum nostrum' ("so that I may go up to our girded people") diverge significantly from the Hebrew, which speaks of trembling in place and an invading people coming up.
notes.3:18: Vulgate 'in Deo Jesu meo' ("in God my Jesus") renders Hebrew 'yishi' ("my salvation") with the proper name Jesus.
notes.3:19: Vulgate 'victor in psalmis canentem' ("the Victor ... singing in psalms") integrates into the closing sentence what in Hebrew is a musical subscription ("For the choirmaster: with stringed instruments").
